what: Information that is MISSING, what it blocks, and exactly what would supply it. Each item says whether the answer is a decision (yours) or a fetch (mine).

questions.question: Is any sportsbook or odds feed licensed for this repository?
questions.why: The market-anchored prior, every edge column and every parlay price depend on a closing line. Without one the model can only be compared with itself.
questions.blocks: market prior, edge columns, parlay pricing, any 'value' claim on the bet surface
questions.would_be_answered_by: A written yes/no plus the feed name, or a decision to publish model numbers with no market comparison.

questions.question: What settles a pick when a game is postponed, abandoned or replayed?
questions.why: All three frozen pre-registrations say 'settle on the official final'. A postponed game has no final, so as written the pick can never settle and never closes. Deciding this after a postponement is exactly what pre-registration exists to prevent.
questions.blocks: every open pick on a game that might be postponed
questions.would_be_answered_by: A void rule (void/stake-back, or cancelled) written into a NEW prereg file before the next slate.

questions.question: Which capture is the schedule of record?
questions.why: Rest, back-to-back and 3-in-4 are computed from a union of three captures (data/origin/games.csv to 11/13, the 11/14 settled feed, the 11/15-11/17 slate). The union works, but a gap at a seam invents a rested team.
questions.blocks: nothing today; a standing integrity risk
questions.would_be_answered_by: A decision to make one daily-refreshed capture authoritative, or to keep unioning with published seams.

questions.question: Is a reference coordinate source acceptable for travel distance?
questions.why: The NBA publishes no arena coordinates. The table is now sourced from the MediaWiki coordinates API and labelled reference, not official.
questions.blocks: whether travel can be used as a model input at all, or only displayed
questions.would_be_answered_by: Accept the labelled reference table, or drop travel from the inputs.

questions.question: What are the final scores of the eight 11/15 games other than IND @ PHI?
questions.why: One pick (HOU @ WAS) has an ended game day and no verified final, so it cannot be graded.
questions.blocks: grading that pick and the leaderboard sample
questions.would_be_answered_by: Two official reads per game: the nba.com game page and the statsdmz game book PDF. Both are fetchable; the game book is the one that takes a per-game fetch.

questions.question: What are the home venues for CHA, GSW and POR?
questions.why: No game hosted by those clubs appears in the 11/15-11/22 official block that was read, so their home venue is not published and their travel rows stay blank.
questions.would_be_answered_by: One official schedule read covering a date on which each club plays at home (e.g. late November).

questions.question: What did the injury reports between 06:15 AM and 7:45 PM ET on 11/15 say?
questions.why: The archive holds 3 of the 76 filings the official index lists for 11/15. A status change between 06:15 a.m. and tip is invisible to the model.
questions.blocks: a true consecutive-report diff across the day
questions.would_be_answered_by: One PDF fetch per filing timestamp; the index lists every one.

questions.question: Does the strategy leaderboard rank anything yet?
questions.why: Three strategies are pre-registered and 11 picks are sealed, but only one has settled, so no strategy has a sample.
questions.would_be_answered_by: Time and settled picks; nothing else is missing.

questions.question: Is the rotation/minutes redistribution a forecast or a demonstration?
questions.why: It is a demonstration: the captured player logs (11/14) and the archived absences (11/15) do not overlap at any club, so there is no absence to redistribute.
questions.would_be_answered_by: Capturing a game book that contains a player who then appears as Out on a later injury report.
